circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Abu Dhabi's Yas Island, has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The circuit represents the second of four Middle Eastern Formula One venues, following Bahrain and preceding Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track encircling Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb, hosting the annual Formula One Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 classification for racing facilities.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: Located in Spielberg, Austria, this 4. 326 km circuit was originally built as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following modifications and a rebranding, the track resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital, stretching 6. 003 kilometers to rank as the fourth-longest Formula One venue. The circuit hosted its first F1 race as the 2016 European Grand Prix, before becoming a permanent calendar fixture under the Azerbaijan Grand Prix name from 2017 onward.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km facility that hosted the first Formula One grand prix ever held in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside other racing series. The venue, which holds a FIA Grade 1 license and features multiple track configurations, has also accommodated international motorsport events including endurance racing and touring cars over its operational history.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, Spain, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya spans 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for competing teams. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: The 7-kilometre Belgian circuit at Spa-Francorchamps has been a mainstay of Formula One racing since 1950, when it featured in the championship's inaugural season. Located near the town of Spa in Wallonia, the venue has hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually from 1985 onwards, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, the Circuit Gilles Villeneuve is a 4. 361 km temporary street circuit that serves as the home of Canada's Formula One Grand Prix. Beyond hosting top-tier single-seater racing, the venue has also accommodated various international motorsport series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, the Shanghai International Circuit is a major motorsport venue most recognized for hosting the Chinese Grand Prix, which ran annually from 2004 to 2019 before resuming in 2024. The track also serves as the home for the Shanghai ePrix, which began competition from 2024 onwards.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is an English racing facility situated in Northamptonshire that has served as the permanent home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, having originally hosted the event in 1948. The track gained further significance when it staged the inaugural World Championship round in 1950, before the Grand Prix alternated between three venues for several decades. Beyond Formula One, the circuit continues to attract major international motorsport events including MotoGP races.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km circuit near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted the first Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc when it opened in 1986, constructed in just eight months, making it the fastest-built Grand Prix venue at the time. Built outside the city near a major highway rather than as a street circuit in Budapest's central park, the inaugural race on 24 March 1986 was dedicated to János Drapál, a pioneering Hungarian motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza is a 5. 793 km Italian racing circuit constructed in 1922 near Milan, earning the nickname "Temple of Speed" for its notably long straights and fast-flowing corners. Since 1949, it has been the home of the Italian Grand Prix, one of Formula One's most prestigious events, making it a historic venue that represents mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing facility.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, situated in Mie Prefecture, Japan, is a 5. 807 km motorsport venue operated by Honda Mobilityland with a spectator capacity of 155,000. The track is primarily recognized as a premier destination for Formula One racing and serves as a regular host for the Japanese Grand Prix on the F1 calendar.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course that navigates through Paradise, Nevada, weaving around the famous Las Vegas Boulevard with its collection of prominent hotels and casinos. The layout incorporates several iconic venues including the MSG Sphere, Caesars Palace, Bellagio, and Paris Las Vegas as it traces a path through the heart of the city's entertainment district.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is named after two Mexican racing brothers who died in separate accidents. The circuit has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix across three distinct periods, with the most recent era beginning in 2015 after a 23-year absence, now branded as the Mexico City Grand Prix since 2021.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens that hosts the Miami Grand Prix. Spanning 3. 363 miles with 19 corners, the track generates qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph and was created by specialist circuit designers for its debut on the Formula One calendar in 2022.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, encircling the harbour in the Principality of Monaco, and is widely known by the name of its primary neighbourhood, Monte Carlo.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259-kilometer track that reclaimed its place on the Formula One calendar in 2021 with the revival of the Dutch Grand Prix. The partnership between the circuit and Formula One is scheduled to conclude in 2026.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is a Qatari motorsport venue situated north of Doha near the city of Lusail, measuring 5. 419 kilometers with a 1. 068-kilometer main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit in São Paulo that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aviation accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track now serves as Pace's final resting place and features an adjacent kart facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The venue also began accommodating Formula E racing in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's Marina Bay area, incorporating the urban districts of Downtown Core and Kallang within its street-based layout.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km circuit features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for racing machinery. The venue accommodates 140,700 spectators and holds FIA Grade 1 certification.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile Grade 1 FIA racing facility that regularly hosts the Formula One United States Grand Prix alongside major motorcycle and endurance racing events. The track has served as home to numerous racing series over the years, including IndyCar, sports car championships, and various international motorsport competitions.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a dual Thai and British driver who currently races for Williams in Formula One, competing under the Thai flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso currently competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 alongside 32 Grand Prix victories throughout his 23-season career. Beyond single-seaters, Alonso has achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, including two Le Mans victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both Formula One and world sportscar titles.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One entry in 2025 and has already claimed six race victories while competing for Mercedes.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver who currently races for Haas, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Gabriel Bortoleto is a Brazilian racing driver currently competing in Formula One as part of the Audi team.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: The Finnish driver currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, having secured two consecutive championship runner-up finishes with Mercedes during 2019 and 2020. Across his 13 seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 10 Grand Prix victories.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine competitor who currently races in Formula One representing Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve position with Haas in Formula One while competing in the European Le Mans Series' LMP2 category with Nielsen Racing. He has started seven Grand Prix events between 2024 and 2025.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory at AlphaTauri remains a significant achievement in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Hadjar is a French-Algerian driver who currently races in Formula One for Red Bull Racing, competing under the French banner.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British driver competing for Ferrari in Formula One, holding an equal record of seven world championship titles alongside Michael Schumacher. He leads the sport's all-time statistics in victories, pole positions, and podium appearances.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races for Audi in Formula One. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved significant success in endurance competition, including a victory at the 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 driving for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand motorsport competitor, currently drives for Racing Bulls in the Formula One championship.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently represents Ferrari in Formula One, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his nine seasons in the sport. Leclerc finished as championship runner-up in 2022, his best result to date in the drivers' standings.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the World Endurance Championship with BMW through WRT, while also driving part-time in NASCAR's top series for Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods, competing from 2014-2020 and again from 2022-2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship title with the team. Over his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 12 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: Esteban Ocon is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Haas. He previously achieved a victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix while competing for Alpine.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez currently races for Cadillac in Formula One. He finished as championship runner-up in 2023 while with Red Bull and has secured six Grand Prix victories throughout his 15-year career in the sport.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Australian driver Oscar Piastri currently races for McLaren in Formula One, having accumulated nine career Grand Prix victories since joining the grid.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by the nickname "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: George Russell is a British Formula One driver currently racing for Mercedes who has secured seven Grand Prix victories during his eight-season career in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz Vázquez de Castro currently races for Williams in Formula One, where he has accumulated four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver currently racing in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category with Proton Competition, following a brief stint in Formula One between 2023 and 2024. Prior to his endurance racing commitments, he competed in IMSA's LMP2 class driving for Era Motorsport.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Canadian driver Lance Stroll currently races for Aston Martin in Formula One, following a career path that has established him as a competitive presence in the sport's premier championship.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently fulfilling a reserve role with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls, having previously competed as a full-time Formula One competitor between 2021 and 2025.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen represents the Netherlands in Formula One while competing for Red Bull Racing, where he has secured four consecutive world championship titles spanning 2021 to 2024. Over his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu represents China as a racing driver currently employed by Cadillac in a reserve capacity. The Beijing-born competitor made his Formula One debut in 2022 and raced through the 2024 season, holding the distinction of being the sole Chinese national to have competed in the sport's top tier.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: Alpine Racing competes from its Enstone base as Renault's official Formula One representative, having been rebranded under the Alpine sports car marque in 2021 after operating as Renault F1 Team. The squad achieved its sole victory in this guise when Esteban Ocon triumphed at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix, before Renault's factory involvement concluded at the end of 2025. Currently powered by Mercedes engines and racing under French colours, the team now features Pierre Gasly and Franco Colapinto as its driver pairing.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin, a British automotive manufacturer, has maintained a presence in Formula One through different incarnations, with the current racing operation competing under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP, the racing arm of the Italian luxury automobile manufacturer, represents the oldest and most accomplished team in Formula One history, competing continuously since the championship's inception in 1950. Known colloquially as "the Prancing Horse" after their iconic emblem, the team has maintained an unbroken presence throughout the sport's entire existence.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: TGR Haas F1 Team is an American-licensed outfit founded by NASCAR team owner Gene Haas that entered Formula One competition in 2016. The team has been led by Ayao Komatsu as principal since January 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who held the position throughout the team's first eight seasons.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: A Swiss engineering firm founded in 1970, the Sauber operation began with sports car construction before joining Formula One as an independent manufacturer in 1993. The team achieved notable endurance racing success, including a Le Mans victory, but after three decades competing in Formula One, exited the championship in 2025 having established itself as one of the sport's longest-running constructors before its acquisition by Audi.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing Limited represents Britain's presence in Formula One, operating from its Woking headquarters and functioning as part of the broader McLaren Group structure under Bahraini ownership through Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes-Benz has maintained a prominent presence in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, competing from its Brackley base under a German licence, operates as a tripartite venture between Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff following a 2022 ownership restructuring. The marque's racing heritage earned it the enduring "Silver Arrows" designation.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that began competing in 2024 as one of two teams owned by Red Bull GmbH, alongside Red Bull Racing. Headquartered in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, the team operates as Red Bull's second constructor in the championship.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced competition in 2024 as part of Red Bull's dual-team structure in the sport. Based in Faenza with additional operations in Milton Keynes, the team operates alongside Red Bull Racing as the second constructor under Austrian ownership Red Bull GmbH.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England that has been operating since 2005 as part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio. Under Christian Horner's management from its inception through 2024, the team established itself as a competitive force in the championship before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, is a British Formula One constructor and team competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026. The outfit emerged following Williams's earlier failed racing venture and operates from its Grove, Oxfordshire headquarters.
